# AgentOS

AgentOS is a local-first, agent-agnostic engineering intelligence layer. It gives coding agents
(Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or any other) the right knowledge, skills, workflow, feedback and
guardrails for a task — without replacing the agent.

> Status: **early development**. The CLI can initialise a project, manage portable skills, build a
> derived knowledge graph, assemble a budgeted Context Pack, and run validation providers. Workflow
> and the other engines are not implemented yet.

## Build

Requirements: Rust (stable, edition 2024) and Git. SQLite is bundled; no system install needed.

```bash
cargo build --release
./target/release/agentos --version
```

## Usage

```bash
agentos init              # create .agentos/ (config, profile, derived SQLite index); safe to re-run
agentos doctor            # check root, git, .agentos, config, database, writability
agentos doctor --json     # same, machine-readable
agentos config            # effective configuration and the source of every value

agentos project profile          # classification, maturity, signals (written by init and scan)
agentos scan                     # index the repository; a second run reports 0 changed
agentos knowledge stats          # node, edge and provenance counts
agentos knowledge nodes          # logical ids
agentos knowledge edges
agentos knowledge inspect <id>
agentos knowledge rebuild        # delete the derived graph and scan again

agentos skills list               # skills that won discovery, with level and invocation
agentos skills inspect tdd        # metadata, resolved dependencies, permissions, body
agentos skills inspect tdd --brief  # metadata only; the body is not read
agentos skills validate           # everything, including bodies; exit 3 on errors
agentos skills install ./my-skill # copy a local skill into .agents/skills/ (git URLs: not yet)
agentos skills graph [--format dot]
agentos domain scan               # infer domain nodes; never confirms them
agentos domain contexts
agentos domain terminology
agentos domain map
agentos domain propose            # one lifecycle step toward Proposed
agentos domain confirm <id>       # Proposed → Confirmed, or Confirmed → Canonical
agentos domain reject <id>
agentos domain validate           # exit 3 when canonical evidence has drifted
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
                              # naive file-token baseline; writes evals/baselines/context-baseline.json
agentos context explain "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos context build "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --format json
agentos context stats "Add retry support to payment webhook processing"
agentos evaluate skills           # run evals/skills; exit 3 if a case fails
agentos evaluate knowledge        # project profiles and language graph fixtures
agentos evaluate ddd              # domain lifecycle fixtures
agentos evaluate context          # context packs against evals/context
agentos validate detect           # providers selected for this project
agentos validate --kind unit_test --json
agentos validate last             # most recently stored result
agentos validate record-regression <id>
                              # write evals/feedback/<id>.json from a failed result
agentos architecture analyze     # detectors over the knowledge graph; exit 3 if any finding
agentos evaluate feedback         # detection, parsing, permission, regressions
agentos evaluate architecture     # bad and good architecture fixtures
agentos plan "Add retry support to payment webhook processing" --workflow feature
agentos run <plan-id> --runner mock
agentos run status <run-id>
agentos run resume <run-id>
agentos run abort <run-id>
agentos evaluate workflow         # plans, scheduler, resume, fix loop
```

Global flags: `--root <PATH>`, `--json`, `-v` / `-vv`, `--log-level <FILTER>`.

### Skills

A skill is a directory with a `SKILL.md`: YAML front-matter (schema:
[`schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json`](schemas/skill-manifest.schema.json)) plus a markdown body.
Discovery locations, highest priority first:

1. `<root>/.agents/skills/`
2. `<root>/.agentos/skills/`
3. user-level: `--user-skills-dir`, else `AGENTOS_USER_SKILLS_DIR`, else `$HOME/.agentos/skills`
4. built-in skills compiled into `agentos` (from `skills/`; replace with `--builtin-skills-dir` /
   `AGENTOS_BUILTIN_SKILLS_DIR`)

A higher level overrides a lower one. Two skills with the same name at the same level are an error,
and a broken skill hides lower-level copies of the same name instead of silently falling back.

Invocation: `user_invocable` (default `true`) and `model_invocable` (default `false`) are separate.
A model-invocable skill may not require, or route to, a skill that is only user-invocable.
Permissions (`fs.read`, `fs.write`, `shell`, `network`, `browser`) are default-deny.

### Project root

`--root` if given, otherwise the Git top-level of the current directory, otherwise the current
directory.

### Configuration

Resolved per key, later layers winning:

1. built-in defaults
2. `.agentos/config.toml`
3. environment: `AGENTOS_LOG` (`log.level`), `AGENTOS_OUTPUT` (`output.format`)
4. CLI flags: `--log-level` / `-v` / `-vv`, `--json`

| Key | Default | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | `warn` | a level (`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`) or tracing directives such as `agentos_core=debug,warn` |
| `output.format` | `text` | `text`, `json` |

Logs are written to stderr; command results to stdout.

### Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | success |
| 1 | runtime error |
| 2 | usage error |
| 3 | a check failed: `doctor` critical failure, `skills validate` errors, `evaluate` case failures, a workflow run that is `failed` or `blocked` |

### Project state

```text
.agentos/
├── config.toml          # project configuration (yours to edit; never overwritten)
├── .gitignore           # keeps derived state out of Git
├── project-profile.json # derived classification and signals; rewritten by init and scan
├── agentos.db           # SQLite knowledge index: derived state, safe to delete and rebuild
├── context-cache/       # derived Context Pack cache
├── feedback/            # derived validation results
└── runs/                # derived plans and resumable runs
```

## Development

```bash
scripts/check.sh   # cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test --workspace
```

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

# AgentOS Evaluation System

Evaluation is a first-class subsystem beginning in Phase 0.

## Test layers

1. Unit tests
2. Integration tests
3. Fixture repository tests
4. Golden/retrieval tests
5. End-to-end workflow evaluations
6. Adapter compatibility tests
7. Regression tests for every discovered defect

## Fixture philosophy

Fixtures are small, realistic repositories with known ground truth. Include multiple technology stacks and deliberately bad architectures.

Recommended fixtures:
- `python-fastapi/`
- `node-express/`
- `typescript-react/`
- `go/`
- `java/`
- `ruby-rails/`
- `bad-architecture/`

## Golden case shape

```json
{
  "task": "Add retry support to payment webhook processing",
  "must_include": ["domain.payment.entity.Payment"],
  "must_not_include": ["fleet", "analytics"],
  "required_fragments": ["webhook_handler.py", "test_webhook_idempotency.py"]
}
```

Exact thresholds are derived from measured baselines, never invented.

## Core metrics

Knowledge: node precision/recall, edge precision/recall, provenance coverage.
DDD: context detection, terminology ambiguity, invariant mapping, lifecycle correctness.
Context: required-context recall, irrelevant-context rate, token count, reduction versus baseline, latency, reproducibility.
Skills: discovery, routing, dependency correctness, permission enforcement.
Feedback: validation detection and structured diagnostics.
Architecture: known-violation detection.
Workflow: execution order, ready frontier, resume behavior, bounded repair loops.
Memory: retrieval precision, staleness, forget semantics, secret redaction.
Adapters: install, idempotency, compatibility, uninstall safety.

## Evaluation traceability

Every context and major workflow evaluation should make it possible to answer:
- what inputs were used?
- what knowledge was selected?
- what was excluded and why?
- what tools/permissions were granted?
- what validation evidence was produced?

## Release gate

A release is green only when the relevant automated tests and evaluations pass, regression coverage remains green, and all phase gates are approved.

## Additions

**Golden case optional fields:** `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are `null` until the Phase 4 baseline has been measured; only then are they set. Cases also record `fixture`, the deterministic oracle used, and (for context cases) `required_fragments`.

**Eval folders:** `evals/{knowledge,ddd,context,skills,workflow,feedback,architecture,memory,adapters,end-to-end,baselines}/`.

**Evaluate intermediate artifacts, not only final code:** project profile, knowledge graph, context pack, plan, permissions, feedback, final changes.

**Regression rule:** every bug becomes a permanent case (e.g. `evals/context/payment_webhook_007.json` for "Notifications context retrieved for a Payment task"). `agentos evaluate <area>` must keep it green.

**Dashboard (Phase 10):** `agentos evaluate` prints Knowledge / DDD / Context / Skills / Feedback / Adapters sections and an overall PASS/FAIL using REAL measured values; thresholds come from `evals/thresholds.json`, derived from baselines.

**Known-bad fixture:** `fixtures/bad-architecture/` (circular dependencies, fat controllers, DB calls in domain, duplicate terminology, broken invariants, shallow modules, missing tests) with ground truth.
# AgentOS Knowledge Model

## Source of truth

The repository remains the source of truth. The knowledge index is derived state.

## Provenance

Every assertion should identify whether it is:

- observed: derived directly from repository/tool output
- declared: explicitly supplied by a human/project artifact
- inferred: model/system interpretation
- generated: derived artifact such as summaries or maps

Do not silently upgrade inferred information to canonical truth.

## Identity

Logical IDs should be stable across source-file moves. Example:

```text
domain.payment.entity.Payment
```

rather than using only a path-based identifier.

## Edge model

Edges should have:

```text
id
from
relation_type
to
confidence
provenance
metadata
```

Useful relations include:

### Domain

- BELONGS_TO
- CONTAINS
- HAS_ENTITY
- HAS_VALUE_OBJECT
- HAS_AGGREGATE
- CONSTRAINED_BY
- GOVERNS
- CROSS_CONTEXT_TO
- ANTI_CORRUPTS

### Software

- IMPLEMENTS
- EXPOSES
- CALLS
- DEPENDS_ON
- IMPORTS
- ADAPTS
- PROVIDES
- CONSUMES

### Quality

- TESTS
- VERIFIES
- VALIDATES
- VIOLATES

### Engineering

- GOVERNED_BY
- JUSTIFIED_BY
- SUPERSEDES
- CONFLICTS_WITH
- DERIVED_FROM

### Agent

- REQUIRES
- PRODUCES
- CONSUMES
- USES_TOOL
- INVOKES

## Fragment model

Fragments are the units that can be included in a Context Pack.

A fragment should contain:

```text
id
node_id
source_ref
location
content
fingerprint
token_estimate
kind
```

Examples:
- a class body
- a function
- a test case
- an ADR section
- a terminology entry
- an architecture rule

## Why fragments matter

A 900-line source file can describe one knowledge node but expose only a 20-line method as the relevant evidence. Nodes describe structure; fragments control context cost.

## Common node envelope

Every node should conceptually contain:

```text
id
node_type
name
scope
summary
status
provenance
confidence
version
fingerprint
source_refs
retrieval_metadata
payload
```
## Core node types

### Domain

- bounded_context
- entity
- value_object
- aggregate
- invariant
- domain_service
- policy
- domain_event
- terminology

### Software

- source_file
- symbol
- module
- interface
- api
- repository
- database_table
- external_service

### Engineering

- adr
- architecture_component
- constraint
- decision

### Quality

- test
- test_suite
- validation

### Agent

- skill
- tool
- capability

### Memory

- task
- episode
- observation
- lesson
- research

# Evaluations

Deterministic evaluation cases, one folder per area (see `docs/spec/EVALUATION.md`):

```text
evals/
├── knowledge/  ddd/  context/  skills/  workflow/  feedback/
├── architecture/  memory/  adapters/  end-to-end/
└── baselines/      # measured baselines; thresholds are derived from these, never invented
```

## Conventions

- One case per file, named `<topic>_<NNN>.json` (e.g. `context/payment_webhook_007.json`).
- Every case names the `fixture` it runs against and the deterministic oracle used.
- Every bug found becomes a permanent regression case in the relevant area.
- No LLM or network calls. Same input must produce the same result.
- `evals/thresholds.json` is introduced only once baselines exist (Phase 4 onward).

## Running

```bash
agentos evaluate skills      # exit 0 if every case passes, 3 if any fails
agentos evaluate knowledge
agentos evaluate ddd
agentos evaluate context
agentos benchmark baseline fixtures/python-fastapi
```

The harness lives in `crates/agentos-evaluation`; `cargo test --workspace` also runs the committed
suite. A case file with an unknown field, an `id` that differs from its file name, or an empty
`oracle` is rejected rather than silently skipped.

## `skills/` (Phase 1)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `manifest` | one skill directory loads (or fails) with exactly the expected diagnostic codes |
| `discovery` | winning level per skill, overrides, exact diagnostic code set |
| `resolve` | exact dependency order, or the expected error code and cycle path |
| `route` | expected top skill (or `null` for none), `must_not_rank`, or a routing error |
| `permission` | `check(skill, capability)` verdict |
| `validate` | full validation outcome, diagnostic codes and (optionally) the exact skill list |
| `skill_eval` | every skill's own `eval_cases` hold (one result per eval case) |

`fixture` is a directory under `fixtures/` (with optional `project/`, `user/`, `builtin/`
subdirectories, or a bare directory of skills), or `builtin:skills` for the shipped skills.

## `knowledge/` (Phase 2 and 2b)

Phase 2: four profile cases and the `python-fastapi` graph. Phase 2b adds graph cases
`node-express`, `typescript-react`, `go`, `java`, and `ruby-rails`. A case `id` is the file stem.

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `profile` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/profile.json` (classification, maturity, confidence, every signal) |
| `graph` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/graph.json` (node id, type, provenance kind; edge endpoints, relation, provenance kind) |

A graph case passes only when both sets match (recall and precision are `n/n`), every node and edge
has complete provenance, a second scan writes zero rows, and deleting `agentos.db` then scanning
reproduces the same node fingerprints. The case copies the fixture before scanning it.

## `ddd/` (Phase 3)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `domain` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain.json` (node id, type, lifecycle, provenance; edge endpoints, relation, provenance; finding id and kind) |
| `markdown` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/domain-markdown/*.md` after `domain scan`, `domain propose`, and `domain confirm` of the case's `confirm` id |

A domain case passes only when all three sets match. The detail line reports node, edge, and finding
precision and recall, plus confirmed and canonical counts (both zero on these cases) and whether
provenance is complete. A markdown case passes when the five generated files match the golden bytes.
No timestamp is part of either oracle.

## `context/` (Phase 4)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `context` | `must_include`, `must_exclude`, `required_fragments` on a Context Pack built from `fixtures/<fixture>` after scan and domain scan |

`relevant_files` is the manual file list for `agentos benchmark baseline`. The context engine does
not read it. `max_tokens` and `max_irrelevant_ratio` are the measured pack size and irrelevant-token
ratio. A bounded-context id in `must_exclude` also rejects every selected node in that package.
Recall of `must_include` and `required_fragments` must be complete. The detail line reports recall,
precision, tokens, irrelevant tokens, latency, and reproducibility.

## `feedback/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `detect` | sorted provider ids, or an error substring for an invalid override |
| `command` | exact argv |
| `parse` | outcome and, for a failure, file and line from a recorded output file |
| `permission` | outcome `refused` and the marker file is not created |
| `regression` | re-parse of the recorded stdout/stderr still matches `expected_outcome` and diagnostics |

Detection is not a successful validation run. Timeout and crash are runner flags. A recorded text
file cannot express them. Those two cases set the flag on the captured output and expect
`timed_out` or `crashed`.

## `architecture/` (Phase 5)

| `kind` | Oracle |
|---|---|
| `architecture` | `fixtures/<fixture>/expected/architecture.json` |

A finding matches an expected item when the detector is the same and `paths` contains the expected
path. The case passes only when false positives and false negatives are both zero and a second
analysis returns the same findings. An empty oracle and an empty report is agreement
(`precision 0/0`, `recall 0/0`). No percentage threshold is applied.

## `workflow/` (Phase 6)

| `kind` | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `graph` | ready frontier, join, and bounded concurrency waves |
| `error` | task-graph cycle, missing skill, and zero concurrency |
| `skill_cycle` | skill dependency cycle through the Phase 1 resolver |
| `permission` | a denied capability blocks the step and does not call the runner |
| `resume` | completed steps are not executed again |
| `abort` | abort is persisted, and a second abort is rejected |
| `context` | one Context Pack per step, declared dependency outputs, unrelated fragments excluded |
| `fix` | a bounded fix loop that passes, and one that exhausts the cap |
| `weaken` | deleting a test, removing a test, or dropping an assertion fails the run |
| `transition` | the legal run and step tables, including every illegal edge |
| `workflow` | feature, bugfix, and refactor definitions, including skip reasons |
| `deterministic` | the same task yields the same plan; `--workflow` wins and the task text stays unchanged |

Cases are synthetic. They do not spawn a validation tool or call a model.

# Fixtures

Small, realistic repositories with known ground truth, used by tests and evaluations.

## Convention

```text
fixtures/<name>/
├── README.md        # what the fixture represents and what it is used for
├── ...              # the repository content itself
└── expected/        # ground truth consumed by tests/evaluations (never read by AgentOS itself)
```

- Fixtures are read-only inputs. Tests that need to modify a fixture copy it first with
  `agentos_testkit::copy_fixture("<name>")`.
- Ground truth is reviewed against the extraction rules before it is committed. `expected/` is listed
  in each fixture's `.agentosignore`, so a scan of the fixture does not index the oracle.

## Fixtures

| Name | Phase | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `placeholder` | 0 | Exercises the fixture loader only. No ground truth beyond its own identity. |
| `skills/` | 1 | Small skill trees for manifest parsing, discovery priority, duplicates, broken overrides, dependency cycles, missing dependencies, version constraints, implicit model invocation and broken built-ins. Ground truth lives in `evals/skills/*.json`; see `skills/README.md`. |
| `empty-project` | 2 | No content signals (README is ignored). Expected: `GREENFIELD` / `EMPTY`, uncertain. |
| `greenfield-specified` | 2 | Specs, docs and a manifest, no source. Expected: `GREENFIELD` / `SPECIFIED`. |
| `existing-project` | 2 | Source, tests, docs and a manifest, no spec. Expected: `EXISTING` / `ESTABLISHED`. |
| `hybrid-project` | 2 | Source and a specification. Expected: `HYBRID` / `ESTABLISHED`. |
| `python-fastapi` | 2, 3 | Payments, users, notifications, tests, ADR, API, database, CI, container. Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. Domain ground truth in `expected/domain.json` (Payment, Money, PaymentAggregate, `amount > 0`). |
| `node-express` | 2b | Same payments shape in JavaScript (ESM, JSDoc, `extends`). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `typescript-react` | 2b | Same payments shape in TypeScript, plus a React card (`implements`, JSX). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `go` | 2b | Same payments shape in Go (struct embedding, interface, composite literals). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `java` | 2b | Same payments shape in Java (`extends`, `implements`, constructors). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `ruby-rails` | 2b | Same payments shape in Ruby (inheritance, YARD, `require_relative`). Graph ground truth in `expected/graph.json`. |
| `python-fastapi-ambiguous` | 3 | Payment, Charge, and Transaction are separate types. Domain eval expects an ambiguity finding and no merge. |
| `hexagonal-leak` | 3 | Order domain imports SQLAlchemy with no accepted exception. |
| `hexagonal-adr` | 3 | The same import, allowed by an ADR. |
| `greenfield-domain` | 3 | Billing requirements and a glossary, no source. Domain nodes are Proposed or Observed, never Confirmed. |

`src/` or `lib/`.
